items.definition: To choose between possibilities after thinking. Word family: decision (noun), decisive (adjective), indecisive (adjective), decisively (adverb).
examples: It was a difficult decision, but she made it quickly.
A decisive goal in the last minute won the match.
I'm hopelessly indecisive when I read a long menu.

items.definition: To try to win or to be better than others. Word family: competition (noun), competitor (person), competitive (adjective), uncompetitive (adjective).
examples: Small shops struggle to compete with online retailers.
He is a very competitive person and hates losing.
Our prices are uncompetitive compared with those abroad.

items.definition: To pay someone to work for you. Word family: employer, employee, employment, unemployment, unemployed, employable.
examples: The factory employs about two hundred people.
Unemployment fell for the third month in a row.
A good CV makes you more employable.

items.definition: To make something new exist. Word family: creation (noun), creator (noun), creative (adjective), creativity (noun), creatively (adverb).
examples: The new factory will create fifty jobs.
She has a very creative approach to problem solving.
Creativity matters more than speed in this role.

items.definition: To be decided by something else; to need. Word family: dependence (noun), dependent (adjective), independent, independence, dependable (reliable).
examples: Whether we go depends on the weather.
Many students gain independence when they leave home.
He is a dependable colleague who never misses a deadline.

items.definition: To achieve what you wanted to do. Word family: success (noun), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb), unsuccessful (adjective).
examples: She succeeded in passing the exam at her first attempt.
Their first campaign was unsuccessful, but the second one worked.
The surgeon successfully repaired the damaged knee.

items.definition: To make or grow something, usually in large amounts. Word family: product (noun), production (noun), producer (noun), productive (adjective), productivity (noun).
examples: The region produces most of the country's olive oil.
Productivity rose after the office moved to a four-day week.
It was a very productive meeting.

items.definition: To be connected with something. Word family: relation (noun), relationship (noun), relative (noun and adjective), related (adjective), unrelated (adjective), relatively (adverb).
examples: The two incidents seem to be unrelated.
The city is relatively quiet at this time of year.
Their relationship has improved a lot.

items.definition: To act in a particular way. Word family: behaviour (noun), misbehave (verb), well-behaved (adjective), behavioural (adjective).
examples: The children behaved perfectly during the long journey.
The teacher praised the pupils for their good behaviour.
The study looked at changes in consumer behaviour.

items.definition: Having the skill, time or chance to do something. Word family: ability (noun), unable (adjective), disabled, enable (verb), inability (noun).
examples: She was unable to attend because of illness.
The new app enables users to pay by phone.
He has a remarkable ability to stay calm.

items.definition: A cause or explanation. Word family: reasonable (adjective), unreasonable (adjective), reasonably (adverb), reasoning (noun), reason (verb).
examples: That is a perfectly reasonable request.
The prices are reasonably low for the area.
I don't follow your reasoning.
